correctness.rationale: For every invertible real 3x3 affine cube, the covariogram is V times the product of the three clipped affine overlap lengths. Integrating over a Euclidean ball removes all positive parts exactly up to r0=1/max||b_i||, giving the degree-six polynomial and the pair integral (8/15)||b_i||||b_j||[sqrt(1-gamma^2)+gamma arcsin(gamma)]. Differentiating f twice yields f''=(1-t²)^(-1/2); its monotone integral ratio supplies globally sharp constants 4/15 and (8/15)(pi/2-1), with equality only for orthogonal rows. At the first threshold, only disjoint caps for maximal row norms clip; unaffected product Q_i>0 by strict Cauchy-Schwarz and their uniform cap-tip convergence. Each of two caps contributes pi Q_i delta³/3, hence positive cubic onset. Equality at r0, ties among maximal norms, and singular-limit (but never actual singular) upper extremizers are handled. Independently checked cube H6=1/6, onset 2pi and angular ratio limits. Finitely many cubature samples do not prove the theorem.
